title: Grand jury declines to indict Cassidy Hutchinson
caption: A federal grand jury in Washington declined the Justice Department's request to indict Cassidy Hutchinson, the former White House aide who was the House Jan. 6 committee's star witness in 2022, according to people familiar with the case. Republican lawmakers had accused her of lying under oath; the charges sought were not made public. It is another setback in the department's cases against Trump critics.

stories.name: Grand jury declines to indict Cassidy Hutchinson
facts: A federal grand jury in Washington declined the Justice Department's request to indict Cassidy Hutchinson, a former aide to Trump chief of staff Mark Meadows, according to people familiar with the proceedings.
A Justice Department lawyer told a magistrate judge at an unrelated hearing on Tuesday that a grand jury had not concurred on a proposed indictment; sources said the defendant was Hutchinson.
Hutchinson was a star witness at the House Jan. 6 committee's 2022 hearings; Republican lawmakers had accused her of lying under oath. The exact charges sought were not made public.
Neither Hutchinson nor the Justice Department commented publicly in the first reports.

artwork.alt: Graphic poster illustration: under a single hanging lamp, anonymous grand jurors sit at a long table around a towering stack of papers representing the proposed indictment, its signature line left blank and a pen set aside. Behind them, a large coral halftone disc recalls Cassidy Hutchinson, with shoulder-length blonde hair, speaking at a witness table microphone during her 2022 Jan. 6 committee testimony. Dark silhouettes frame the foreground.
